transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m having trouble keeping my attention where it’s supposed to be at work. I’ll be on a grant call or in a safety meeting, and then I notice some pump vibration, or a student says something offhand, or I remember an odd peak in an old spectrum… and I’m gone. I’ll chase that for hours, and the thing people actually needed from me just falls apart.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're sitting still?

Yes. I don’t just… sit well. I’ll get into the lab before anyone else and start moving things around—protocols, instrument schedules, emails, analyses. It feels like if I stop, I’m wasting the chance to get everything fixed.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?
I don’t know. I mean… I can make quick decisions, but I wouldn’t say I’m always just acting without thinking. It depends what you mean.
Do you often interrupt others when they're speaking?
I’m not sure. I probably do sometimes, especially if I think I know where someone’s going, but I haven’t really tracked it.
Do you have trouble waiting for your turn in line or in other situations?
I’m not really sure. Lines annoy me, but I don’t know that it’s more than anyone else. I usually just… try to get through it.
Do you have trouble organizing tasks and managing your time effectively?

Yeah… lately, yes. It’s been a problem at work. I used to handle certain project decisions myself, but my department has had to step in more because I’ve missed priorities and gotten schedules mixed up. It’s… not great, especially with supervision and lab safety expectations.
Do you often talk more than others in social situations?
I don’t really know. I’m not usually thinking about it in the moment. Maybe sometimes, but I haven’t noticed it as a pattern.
Do you have trouble controlling your emotions when you're stressed or upset?

Yes… I guess I do. When things are stressful, especially at the lab, I feel like everything is moving fast and it finally makes sense to me. But if someone questions what I’m doing or tells me to slow down, I can snap. I don’t like admitting that. Some of the students have started avoiding my office.
Have you always had trouble with attention and restlessness, or did it start more recently?
More recently. I mean… I wasn’t always like this. It’s been about seven months, since I took over that multi-site spectroscopy project.
Have your symptoms been causing problems in your relationships with coworkers or family members?

Yes. Mostly at work. My department has… had to step in more than they used to. Decisions I normally handled got messy — priorities were missed, scheduling got confused, supervision got strained. They said it was starting to affect the project, and even some lab safety expectations. I don’t like talking about it.
Were you often restless or fidgety as a child?
I don’t really know. I don’t remember being that way, and no one ever made a point of telling me I was.
Have you noticed any periods in your life where you didn't have these attention and restlessness problems?
Before this project, yes. It really started about seven months ago, when I took over the multi-site spectroscopy work. Before that, I don’t think it was an issue.
Did you engage in a lot of physical activity or sports as a child?
Not really sure. I mean, I did normal school activities, but I wasn’t especially into sports or anything that I remember.
Do you ever find yourself so focused on something that you forget about everything else around you?
I’m not sure. I mean, I can get absorbed in work sometimes, but I don’t know that I’d say I forget everything around me.
Have you experienced significant symptoms of inattention, such as making careless mistakes or having difficulty sustaining attention in tasks, outside of work or the lab?

Mostly in work settings, but not just the bench itself. Like on a grant call or in a safety meeting, I’ll hear a pump vibration or someone makes a side comment, and then my mind just… goes there. Or I’ll remember some odd peak from an old spectrum and lose hours chasing it. Meanwhile the actual thing I was supposed to handle kind of falls apart.
Do you experience these problems with attention and restlessness at home or in your free time, not just at work?

It’s mostly noticeable around the lab or work stuff. I mean… even if I’m technically not at the bench, like on a grant call or in a safety meeting, something small pulls me off—a pump noise, a side comment, some old data point—and then I’m gone chasing that for hours. That’s really what brought me in.
Do you experience restlessness or attention problems when you're not working or in the lab?

Not as much when I’m away from work. It’s really the lab-related stuff that does it… like a grant call, a safety meeting, some pump noise or a student’s comment, and then I’m chasing that instead of the actual experiment. Then the thing people were waiting on from me just… doesn’t get done right.
Are your symptoms of inattention and restlessness ever present when you are on vacation or completely removed from work-related activities?

On vacation? Not really, or at least I don’t notice it the same way. What made me come in is that at work I can’t keep my mind on the actual experiment anymore. Even in a grant call or safety meeting, some pump vibration or a comment or an old spectrum peak pulls me off, and then I’m chasing that for hours while the thing everyone needs from me falls apart.
Are your symptoms ever present when you're engaged in hobbies or activities you enjoy outside of work?

Not really with hobbies, no. It’s more… the work stuff. Like I said, during a grant call or a safety meeting I’ll catch a pump vibration or someone’s side comment, or remember some odd peak from an old spectrum, and then I’m off on that for hours. The actual experiment, the thing people are waiting on, just falls apart.
Have you experienced any significant symptoms of anxiety or depression?
I… I’m not sure. I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed anything big like that, at least not clearly. It’s hard for me to separate from everything else.
